sounds.intro: Esperanto is 100% regular. Every letter has one sound. The stress always falls on the second-last syllable.
notes: Nouns end in -o, adjectives in -a, adverbs in -e, verbs in -as (present), -is (past), -os (future). Plural: add -j. Object: add -n.
There is no gender, no irregular verbs and no articles except "la" (the).

phrases.title: Formal and informal
items: ĉu vi bonvolus paroli la anglan?
choo vee bon-VO-loos pa-RO-lee la AN-glan
phrases.note: Esperanto has one word for "you": vi. There is a rarely used informal "ci", but nobody needs it. For politeness, use "bonvolu", "sinjoro" (sir) and "sinjorino" (madam).

vocab.title: Common verbs
vocab.note: Dictionary form ends in -i. The present tense is -as for every person: mi estas, vi estas, li estas.

vocab.title: School verbs
vocab.note: Shown in the dictionary form, which ends in -i.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Mi (I), vi (you, one or many), li (he), ŝi (she), ĝi (it), ni (we), ili (they), oni (one, people in general). The pronoun is always needed, because the verb does not change.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: The plural ends in -j: libro, libroj. The object adds -n: mi vidas la libron. The only article is "la" (the), the same for everything. There is no word for "a".

grammar.title: Esti: to be
text: Esti is the only verb "to be". It does not change: mi estas, vi estas, li estas, ni estas, ili estas. Past: estis. Future: estos.

grammar.title: Havi: to have
text: Havi (to have) is regular: mi havas, vi havas, li havas. For hunger, Esperanto has its own verb: malsati.

grammar.title: Verbs: present tense
text: Every verb has the same ending in the present tense, for every person: -as. Take the infinitive (-i) and change it to -as. Parolas = speak/speaks.

grammar.title: Iri: to go
text: Iri (to go) is regular. To say you are about to do something, use the future: mi manĝos (I will eat). To suggest "let us", use ni + -u: ni iru!

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order: subject, verb, object, as in English. The adjective can come before or after the noun. Word order is flexible, because the -n shows the object.
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put "ne" before the verb. Other negatives: neniu (nobody), nenio (nothing), neniam (never). Always compare with the positive form.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Start the sentence with "ĉu" to make a yes-or-no question. The rest stays the same.

grammar.title: Question words
text: All start with ki-: kio (what), kiu (who / which), kie (where), kiam (when), kial (why), kiel (how), kiom (how much), kia (what kind).

grammar.title: Possessives
text: Add -a to the pronoun: mi, mia (my); vi, via (your); li, lia (his); ŝi, ŝia (her); ni, nia (our); ili, ilia (their). They take -j and -n like adjectives.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: Esperanto has no formal "you". Use "vi" for everybody. Add "sinjoro" (sir), "sinjorino" (madam), "bonvolu" (please) for politeness.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: change -i to -is. Future: change -i to -os. Conditional: -us. The same for every person.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Change -i to -u for a command. It is the same for one person or many: venu! Make it negative with "ne": ne venu!

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Povi (can), devi (must), voli (want) are followed by the infinitive: mi povas naĝi. "Ne rajti" = not allowed.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: en = in, sur = on, sub = under, apud = next to, proksime de = near, ĉe = at / by, je = at (time).
ex: the book is on the table
la libro estas sur la tablo
la LEE-bro ES-tas soor la TA-blo
the cat is under the table
la kato estas sub la tablo
la KA-to ES-tas soob la TA-blo
the shop is next to the bank
la butiko estas apud la banko
la boo-TEE-ko ES-tas A-pood la BAN-ko
the park is near the station
la parko estas proksime de la stacidomo
la PAR-ko ES-tas PROK-see-me de la sta-tsee-DO-mo
la leciono estas je la naŭa
la le-TSEE-o-no ES-tas ye la NOW-a
the key is in the bag
la ŝlosilo estas en la sako
la shlo-SEE-lo ES-tas en la SA-ko

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: pli ... ol = more ... than. plej = the most. malpli = less. The same for every adjective: pli bona (better), plej bona (best).
ex: ĉi tio estas pli bona ol tio
CHEE TEE-o ES-tas plee BO-na ol TEE-o
ĉi tio estas pli malbona ol tio
CHEE TEE-o ES-tas plee mal-BO-na ol TEE-o
ŝi estas pli alta ol mi
shee ES-tas plee AL-ta ol mee
Taŝkento estas pli granda ol Samarkando
tash-KEN-to ES-tas plee GRAN-da ol sa-mar-KAN-do

grammar.title: Everyday sentences
text: Extra practice with the most useful patterns.
ex: ĉu ĉi tio estas via libro?
choo CHEE TEE-o ES-tas VEE-a LEE-bro
